content_metadata.description: A video tutorial by a Camper demonstrating how to set tent pegs into hard ground.

qAndA.answer: He modifies an 8mm rotary hammer bit.
qAndA.question: What type of drill bit does the Camper modify?

qAndA.answer: He uses an angle grinder with a 1mm cutting disc.
qAndA.question: What tool does the Camper use to cut the end off the drill bit?

qAndA.answer: The fine dust created by the drilling falls back into the hole, preventing the peg from being inserted.
qAndA.question: Why does the first drilling attempt fail to allow peg placement?

qAndA.answer: He drills the hole and immediately inserts the peg before the dust has a chance to fall back in.
qAndA.question: How does the Camper overcome the problem with the fine dust?

qAndA.answer: The video starts with curiosity, shifts to confusion and frustration when the initial attempts fail, and ends with content as the solution is successfully demonstrated.

youtube_description:
We are travelling around Australia and on occasions have found the Caravan Parks and Camp Grounds sometimes use road base type materials as the camping base. This stuff is like concrete and you'll bend your tent pegs trying to hammer them in. So what do you do if you can't hammer in your pegs?

This video show how we deal with the hard ground at the Shark Bay Caravan Park, which is an awesome place to stay BTW (No, they didn't sponsor us :-) ). I carry some battery powered Makita tools that often come in handy, as you'll see.
